title: Crime and Punishment
subtitle: Another bullet bearing another name falls into a tumbling brass bag.

items.text: Crime and Punishment

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman I
items.text: Raise your glass to the Zeno Cavalry Corps!

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: To the Corps! To the Flying Witches! And to Bereggrad!
Oak mugs meet in a toast, golden liquor overflowing at their rims.

items.speaker: Alpha Four
items.text: To everyone!

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman II
items.text: Hmm, this is nothing like the samogon we brew in the village.

items.speaker: Alpha Four
items.text: Too fiery for you?

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman II
items.text: Not fiery enough!
He drains his mug and lets out a hearty laugh.

items.speaker: Zeno Cavalryman II
items.text: Hit me!
Lilya sits with the celebrants, cheeks flushed, but her eyes still sharp on the sich gates outside the tent.
When she sees the Gryphon soldiers leaving in twos and threes, she spits, picks up her broom, and strides out.

items.speaker: Alpha Four
items.text: Where are you going, Commander? You're the star of this party!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Come on, quit with the titles. Lilya's just fine.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I'm just going to get some more drinks from the city.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Oho, flying under the influence? You sure?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Catch me if you can.
The engine flares orange. Her new broom, carrying Lilya and the name Red 38, shoots into the clouds and disappears.
The commander examines the trail toward Bereggrad with a puzzled look. Then he lifts the tent flap and steps inside.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Where's Lieutenant Lilya off to?

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: The city. Said she'll bring back more drinks.
Weighing the bottle in his hand, he lapses into silence.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I'm afraid there won't be any judgment for me, Lieutenant Lilya.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Oh yeah? What's got you so confident?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: This war between Manus Vindictae and the Foundation will grind on for a long time to come. They won't give the order to arrest me until it ends.
The gun presses harder against his head.
An arcanist's skull is like any other. It has no defense against a bullet.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: They might call us traitors, but still, our names and faces are listed as martyrs in Zeno's Hall of Merit. They know that others doubt, and they fear for their morale.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: They know I still live, of course. Even so, the Foundation gains nothing from making an enemy of me, so long as I remain a potential ally.
The threat brings him no fear. He only answers her anger with measured calm.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: And as a result of my actions in São Paulo, the rift between the Foundation and the various factions of Zeno has been laid bare.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Rift?
Zeno should have been at the front lines of this war with Manus Vindictae, yet the joint command sent them to the Eastern Front.
Lilya knows he speaks the truth.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Huh. So if the Foundation put you on trial, it'd be like they're spitting in Zeno's face.
She looks up at the sky despite herself.
The Flying Witches she put on patrol pass overhead. Their gray and white Foundation uniforms make them look like fluttering doves.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: But the Pax House will intervene.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Even if their direct intervention would sever all trust between the Foundation and Zeno?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Sever all trust? How?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The last thing Zeno wants is to relive the shame of São Paulo. Likewise, the Foundation has no desire to reveal how deep their network goes.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: If the Pax House intervenes, that delicate balance will crumble.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Wait, network? Do you mean the soldiers you "dealt with" in São Paulo?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Ten humans and four arcanists refused to join our rebellion.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Three were spies we had long sniffed out. As for the rest ...
Igor closes his eyes. He won't defend himself any further.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Ahhh!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Bulls**t! They were all our comrades, every one of them!
A trembling finger tightens on the trigger.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: They fought together with you! Shared their canteens and rations with you!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: You could've sent them off somewhere! Could've arrested them, knocked them out, put them to sleep! You had a million ways to pull off your rebellion without killing them!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: You chose to murder them! Why?
The old man's breath doesn't hasten, but his chest heaves.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The Apostles Brotherhood was watching.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: To reach a future free from meaningless sacrifices, some cost must be paid.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: So, you used them, ended them so you could go on with the Manus!

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Yes.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: You'll pay for what you did!

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I've committed many crimes. I will not run from them. I will be ready to surrender my life when the day comes.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: But it has not come. Until it does, I will continue to assist the Timekeeper. Her fight is only just beginning.
The wind drops and the grassland falls still. Only the young pilot's breath grows heavier.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Motherf**ker!
She flings the revolver to the ground, the wild grass swallowing it.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Of all the goddamned arrogance! You're ready to die? No, your death won't fix anything!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: What about everyone who decided to follow you, huh? What about Lopera? You owe her an explanation!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Damn it! You were right about this old fart, Ivan.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: He's got a screw loose in the brain. Someone should send him to Mesmer Jr. to sort him out!
The commander steps out from behind a rise. Clearly he has been watching, unseen, from the start.
He studies Igor, searching for a trace of the past in his weathered eyes.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: You are a madman, Igor.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Except Manus Vindictae, who else dares challenge Zeno and the Foundation?

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: And now, even the Manus march against you. Your Legion walks amid tigers.
Igor turns to his old friend with an unusual calm, as if he weren't sinking into a mire.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Amid tigers? No.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: My Legion soars high above, like the indomitable gryphon.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: My children will rend their foes with claws and guard their friends with wings, and they will bear the ark safely through the currents of time.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Don't flatter yourself.
Lilya spits.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Nothing you do will ever be enough to atone for what you've done.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Agreed. Still, none can deny his deeds in Antarctica and Bereggrad.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Antarctica ...

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I heard from the captain that Ulrich bypassed the Manus troops thanks to Lieutenant Moldir.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: That your order?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: No. This was Moldir's choice. I did not intervene, true, but I cannot take any credit for it.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: *sigh* Stubborn old fart.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: If you step even one toe out of line, you're dead.
She mounts her broom. Before starting the engine, she looks back at Igor.
She points up at the Flying Witches in the clouds.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: We'll be watching you. I will be watching you.
Igor responds with a slow nod.
A shapeless anger sits in Lilya's chest. She snorts and tears into the sky.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: We were just like her once.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Young, unable to ignore anything we saw as unjust, compelled to personally right every wrong.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: But we never put our lives on the line like her, did we? Ah, wait.
The scar on his brow moves with his smile. Memory does live in those old eyes.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: You did.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: So did you.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I never thought an old cat like you would change his spots. Not a change I favor, mind.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: A river turns foul when it halts. We must all find our way to the ocean.
Igor steps toward the river, his boot spurs cutting lines in the soft mud at the bank.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I suspect you were the one that persuaded the lieutenant to leave her gun unloaded.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I owed you for what you did for the Corps.
The commander runs an agitated hand through his hair and joins Igor.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Got a cigarette?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I quit back in 99.
The famed commander of the Zeno Cavalry pulls a handful of grass from a nearby tuft.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Do you have any idea how many of my silly pups wish to follow you after Tamarovka?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I've found a place, somewhere big enough to welcome you and the Corps.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I'm not ready to have a bounty on my head.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: But you spoke in this bounty target's defense. What did you say to Lieutenant Lilya?

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I gave her a choice: end your life with a bullet, or let you live bearing the pain of your guilt.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Did you ever consider that I might just be a cold-hearted tyrant? That I feel no guilt at all?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: We've all changed since the "Storm."

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I read your letter, old friend.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: No truth serum could tell me more than it did.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: "I tarnished with my own hands the honor we once held dear."

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: "Molly, please tell Lopera that—"
A dark arcane glow appears by the letter. A shadowy mouth emerges from it, chews it down, and drags it into the void.
The jar in Igor's hand flickers. A firefly dims and falls to the bottom.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Really? Running your old bones deeper into the ground just to protect your privacy?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Ha, privacy. I thought you'd never heard of the word!

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I didn't mean to pry. The soldiers were getting their letters. Yours was the only one with no name.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: We ride out come morning. We all know that many of us will never return.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: You still have a chance to come to the sich before we leave.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: You want me to take those young soldiers in?

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: This was never meant to be their war.
Lilya's aircraft has left a lingering line across the sky.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: They deserve to see the new spring.
Five days later
Inside the Suitcase

items.speaker: Irinei
items.text: Located in a Foundation facility, completely confidential, and no field mission application required. You're more thoughtful than I expected, Timekeeper.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Let's make the most of our time, Mr. Irinei, before our absence draws unnecessary attention.

items.speaker: Irinei
items.text: Then let's cut to the chase.

items.speaker: Irinei
items.text: About the vessel ensoulment experiments conducted in the Amber Room laboratory.

items.speaker: Irinei
items.text: What have you learned?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I managed to recover documents detailing the experiment's main procedures. However ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I didn't find anything signiﬁcant about Urd.
